cohort: The study included 60 healthy term pregnant women aged 18-40, ASA I-II, undergoing elective C-sections, evenly distributed into general anesthesia and spinal anesthesia groups.
finding: S100b concentrations slightly increased after C-section in both general and spinal anesthesia groups, but without a statistically significant difference between the two anesthesia types.
mod_finding: The form of anesthesia (general vs. spinal) for C-section was found to be irrelevant for S100b levels, indicating no significant difference in brain injury biomarker between these modes of delivery.
cross-section timing: Pre- and post-surgery (maternal blood), and at birth (umbilical artery blood)
